This item asks whether a lone commit of test lines with no Red-run trailer is refused or only warned. It does not block the PR.
Goal: a lane learns it needs a Red-run trailer before its first commit, not after, so no pushed history is rewritten (max efficiency, no waste, owner 20:17 CST Nov 14).
Problem (rule): step red-run-warn-before-commit says warning. The guard only refuses or asks, so PR 3496 refuses a lone git commit that adds test lines with no valid Red-run trailer. The step's word and the built behaviour differ, so it needs your word.
Based on (read): PR 3496 body, GitHub read by triage 04:48 CST (open, draft, head 82245ac5eca1): refusal lives in conflict_markers_hit (hooks/guard_merge.py), judged by lint/check_red_run.py; push check unchanged except a pending revert-line commit is no longer judged (decision red-run-trailer-on-test-commits, rule 7). Coordinator's hand-in message 04:47 CST, relayed.
Based on (read): five notes in docs/debts/notes.md (unstage false refusal, --trailer unread, cost sentence, no scratch exemption, none: reason wording): the lane's reads, triage did not check them.
Departs from: the step says warning; the guard refuses a lone git commit that adds test lines with no valid Red-run trailer.
Who recommends what: the coordinator recommends (a): a warning a lane scrolls past is a spent guard. No ruling found on warning versus refuse for this trailer (triage searched roadmap/rulings).
UPDATE 07:33 CST Nov 15: main now has REFUSE. PR 3496 merged at 07:30:41 CST (GitHub read by triage 07:32 CST), the coordinator's recommended option a, before any owner answer. This item still stands: it now asks whether to keep refuse or change main to warn only. Choosing (a) changes nothing (the step's word 'warning' is rewritten to 'refuse'); choosing (b) means a follow-up change to main. The option texts below were written before the merge: read 'PR 3496 merges as built' as 'already merged' and 'the PR waits' as 'a follow-up lane'. The owner has typed nothing.
